study type: Predictive modeling study using retrospective registry data
exposure: Features available at the time of decision-making on labour induction
outcome: Mode of delivery (cesarean delivery, spontaneous birth, vaginal operative delivery)
cohort: Low-risk nulliparous women with prolonged pregnancies (at or beyond 41 gestational weeks) derived from the nationwide Swedish Medical Birth Register (1998-2019).
finding: Although the considered features lacked strong predictive power for mode of delivery, the study provides valuable methodological information for predicting the timing of labour induction beyond 41 gestational weeks.
mod_finding: The study developed machine learning models to predict mode of delivery (cesarean delivery, spontaneous birth, vaginal operative delivery) in low-risk nulliparous women with prolonged pregnancies.
